answer: Each identity locks 100 credits and posts one signed work proof per epoch to a mesa ledger of proofs. A crystal auditor compares each new proof against the earlier proof from the same key; a second, contradictory proof burns 30 credits and freezes the identity for one epoch. The k-th fake still needs a 100-credit stake and proof, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits and risk 30,000 in slashes, with no shared stake. A rented stake fails because the slash follows the signing key, not the funder. An honest agent posts one proof, keeps its stake and full yarrow reward share.
